- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase downward bias or add early correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast growth rate by 20–30% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often drifts toward mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >5% error), apply “early correction” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence in initial period.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — if sentiment changes sharply, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
